The handle returned by `setTimeout` and `setInterval`.

`refresh()` resets the delay so that it counts from now, and returns the timeout. It also works on a timeout that has already fired, which then fires again after its delay. Before v3.2.4, refreshing a fired timeout did not re-arm the native timer, so the callback did not run on time. It ran only when the native timer next woke for another timer, or not at all when no other timer was pending and the process exited first.
